common_it_words.title: Common IT Words Knowledge Check
common_it_words.summary: A short, low-stakes check on beginner IT vocabulary.

questions.prompt: What is the best beginner-friendly meaning of a domain?

choices.label: A managed environment for accounts, computers, and access

questions.feedback: A domain helps IT manage accounts, computers, and access in an organized way.

questions.prompt: An asset tag helps identify a specific piece of equipment.
questions.feedback: Asset tags help avoid mix-ups when tracking, moving, or documenting equipment.

questions.prompt: What should you do when you hear an IT term you do not know?

choices.label: Pretend you understand and keep going
Ask for the password connected to the term
Write it down and ask a mentor to explain it
Change the setting so you can learn faster

questions.feedback: Writing down unfamiliar terms and asking clear questions is expected beginner behavior.

what_does_it_do.title: What Does IT Do? Knowledge Check
what_does_it_do.summary: A short, low-stakes check on the role of an IT department.

questions.prompt: Which answer best describes IT support work?

choices.label: Helping people, systems, devices, and workflows work safely
Making every decision without asking anyone

questions.feedback: IT work includes people, systems, equipment, documentation, safety, and escalation.

questions.prompt: A new work-study student should know their escalation path before trying unfamiliar tasks.
questions.feedback: Knowing when and who to ask keeps the student, department, and users safer.

questions.prompt: What is a good first response when a user reports a problem you have not seen before?

choices.label: Document what they reported and ask a mentor for the next step
Guess which admin tool might fix it
Tell the user the issue is solved

questions.feedback: Clear documentation plus mentor escalation is a safe beginner response.

domain_basics.title: Domain Basics Knowledge Check
domain_basics.summary: A short, low-stakes check on domain concepts and safe boundaries.

questions.prompt: In a managed IT environment, what can a domain help organize?

choices.label: User accounts, computers, and access rules

questions.feedback: Domains commonly help manage accounts, computers, policies, and access.

questions.prompt: A new student should change domain settings if they think a login problem is domain-related.
questions.feedback: Domain changes are not beginner-safe. Document the issue and ask a mentor.

questions.prompt: What information is useful to document for a possible domain login issue?

choices.label: The exact message, device, user, and time reported
A guess about who caused it

questions.feedback: Useful notes include observable details, not passwords or guesses.

configuration_manager_overview.title: Configuration Manager Knowledge Check
configuration_manager_overview.summary: A short, low-stakes check on Configuration Manager concepts.

questions.prompt: What is the safest beginner-level understanding of Configuration Manager?

choices.label: A tool mentors may use to manage computers and software
A tool students should use to bypass approval
A replacement for tickets and notes

questions.feedback: The module gives a mental model of the tool without authorizing unsupervised use.

questions.prompt: Understanding what Configuration Manager is can help a student follow mentor explanations.
questions.feedback: Knowing the terms makes shadowing and documentation easier.

questions.prompt: What should a student do before taking action in a management tool?

choices.label: Try the action first, then tell someone
Make changes only if a user is waiting
Confirm they are trained, approved, and supervised for that action
Use the most powerful option available

questions.feedback: Training, approval, and supervision matter before using administrative tools.

imaging_overview.title: Computer Imaging Knowledge Check
imaging_overview.summary: A short, low-stakes check on imaging concepts and escalation.

questions.prompt: What is computer imaging, at a beginner level?

choices.label: Taking a photo of a computer
Preparing a computer with an approved standard setup
Guessing which software a user wants

questions.feedback: Imaging is about applying an approved setup, not improvising.

questions.prompt: If an imaging process shows an error, a beginner-safe response is to stop and ask a mentor.
questions.feedback: Imaging errors can affect data, devices, or deployment steps, so escalation is appropriate.

questions.prompt: Which note is most useful after an imaging issue?

choices.label: At 10:15, device ABC123 showed error text during the imaging step
I think the computer is bad

questions.feedback: Specific time, device, and observed message help a mentor troubleshoot safely.

ticket_basics.title: Ticket Basics Knowledge Check
ticket_basics.summary: A short, low-stakes check on tickets and documentation habits.

questions.prompt: What is a ticket mainly used for?

choices.label: Tracking a request or issue and the work done on it

questions.feedback: Tickets help IT track context, progress, ownership, and history.

questions.prompt: A beginner can practice drafting ticket notes even before they are approved to update real tickets.
questions.feedback: Drafting notes is useful practice. Updating real tickets still depends on training and approval.

questions.prompt: Which draft note is strongest?

choices.label: User said monitor shows No Signal. Checked power and cable. Escalating to mentor.

questions.feedback: Strong notes are factual, specific, and clear about escalation.

asset_tag_basics.title: Asset Tag Basics Knowledge Check
asset_tag_basics.summary: A short, low-stakes check on asset tags and equipment tracking.

questions.prompt: Why do asset tags matter?

choices.label: They help identify and track specific equipment
They show which student owns the equipment

questions.feedback: Asset tags make equipment tracking and documentation more reliable.

questions.prompt: If an asset tag is missing or unreadable, you should document it and ask what to do next.
questions.feedback: A missing or unclear tag should be documented instead of guessed.

questions.prompt: Which detail is safest to include in an equipment note?

choices.label: The asset tag, room, device type, and observable condition
A guess about where the device belongs

questions.feedback: Use observable equipment details and avoid private or guessed information.

hardware_basics.title: Hardware Basics Knowledge Check
hardware_basics.summary: A short, low-stakes check on safe hardware observations.

questions.prompt: Which action is beginner-safe for a monitor showing No Signal?

choices.label: Open the computer case and remove parts
Check whether the monitor has power and the cable appears connected

questions.feedback: Observable power and cable checks are beginner-safe; deeper changes need mentor guidance.

questions.prompt: If a device smells burned or appears damaged, stop and escalate.
questions.feedback: Possible damage or safety concerns should be handled by trained staff.

questions.prompt: What should you document before asking for help with a hardware issue?

choices.label: Only that the equipment is broken
The device, location, what the user reported, and safe checks already done
The private login details for the device
A guess about which part failed

questions.feedback: Mentors need clear observed details and the safe checks already attempted.

how_to_ask_for_help.title: How to Ask for Help Knowledge Check
how_to_ask_for_help.summary: A short, low-stakes check on mentor-ready questions.

questions.prompt: Which help request is easiest for a mentor to act on?

choices.label: I checked power and cable on monitor ABC123; it still says No Signal. What should I try next?

questions.feedback: A strong request includes context, safe checks tried, and a clear next-step question.

questions.prompt: Asking for help is part of safe beginner IT work.
questions.feedback: Good escalation protects users, systems, and the student.

questions.prompt: What should you include when you are stuck?

choices.label: What you were trying to do, what happened, what you checked, and your question

questions.feedback: A complete stuck summary helps a mentor respond quickly.

escalation_rules.title: Escalation Rules Knowledge Check
escalation_rules.summary: A short, low-stakes check on when to stop and ask for help.

questions.prompt: When should a student escalate?

choices.label: When a task touches access, data, safety, unfamiliar tools, or unclear approval
Only after trying every possible fix
Never, because asking slows work down
Only when the user is upset

questions.feedback: Escalation is expected when safety, access, data, authority, or unfamiliar steps are involved.

questions.prompt: Stopping to ask a mentor can be the correct action.
questions.feedback: Safe IT work values good judgment, not guessing.

questions.prompt: What is the best next step if you are unsure whether you are allowed to do something?

choices.label: Do it quickly before anyone notices
Ask a mentor or supervisor for approval before proceeding
Ask the user to approve it

questions.feedback: Approval and supervision should be clear before taking unfamiliar or sensitive actions.
